<!--
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
-->

# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the hardware layer (`hal/`) of the
  Felucca firmware, hugelton/Felucca, licensed GPL-3.0 (docs/EXPOSURE.md,
  "Corrections", 2026-10-23). Builds the test harness and writes
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only (addresses, bits, pins, timings,
  protocols), never code or code structure, each fact citing a non-GPL
  source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together). Since
M4 it fails a call that accesses listed material (reads, lists, searches,
fetches or checks it out) and logs, report only, one that only mentions it
(sessions/README.md).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **One list of the spec-side folders.** `config/spec-side-folders` names
  the three folders once (since M3). The barrier tools build every name,
  pattern and exclusion from it, and their tests use made-up names
  (`tests/helpers.py`), so changing them needs no command that names the
  folders. Scratch test repositories made by hand use the made-up names
  too. The deny lists keep their literal paths (Claude Code's syntax), and
  C-UNIT checks they cover every folder on the list and that no barrier
  tool or test spells one out.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
Since M4b the terms of the vendored Plaits (`vendor/plaits/`, read only from
its checksum-verified files) are public like the SDK's, the check says how
many emulator terms that takes off, and `vendor/plaits/` itself is not
scanned, except its `SOURCE.md`, which we write (R-SEP-1).

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

the people who write ours.

  chip model was partly written from the hardware layer (`hal/`) of the
  Felucca firmware, hugelton/Felucca, licensed GPL-3.0 (docs/EXPOSURE.md,
  "Corrections", 2026-10-23). Builds the test harness and writes
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only (addresses, bits, pins, timings,
  protocols), never code or code structure, each fact citing a non-GPL
  source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding

  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL

  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there

  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.

and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in

  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only

  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;

  opens or lists the spec side's transcripts for it, and the check prints
  only how many files it exempted per folder. Every file added or changed
  after the base is checked in full. Files that sessions keep editing get no
  exemption: their current text is redacted instead (`docs/EXPOSURE.md` was,

  username anywhere it appears, the local top-level folder as `<top>`, and
  every private term.

and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh

    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),

  began before its folder had the banner hook;
- for clean-side transcripts, every file read, write, search, web fetch, web
  search and shell command is listed in the check's log by entry (the
  transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and any that touches
  forbidden material fails, named by rule ID (`F-...`, the check's
  `FORBIDDEN` table). The log never quotes a transcript: it goes into every
  test record, and the oldest archived transcripts still hold text that the

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none. Session SR-1-SR-2 (spec side, 2026-10-22) added sections 9 to 11 for
SR-1 and SR-2, which are answered in part; what stays open is Q-2, Q-13
and Q-14. Session SR-3 (spec side, 2026-10-23) added section 12 for SR-3,
answered in part (open: Q-6, Q-15), and section 13, which confirms HW-41's
fwtest part for M3. Session SR-4-6 (spec side, 2026-10-23) added section 14
for SR-5 and SR-6, answered in part (open: Q-16 to Q-18). Session SR-7
(spec side, 2026-10-24) added section 15 for SR-7 (open: Q-19). Session
midi-in-out (spec side, 2026-10-24) added section 16 for SR-8, answered in
part (open: Q-12), and section 17 for MIDI output (open: Q-20). Session
pin-050 (spec side, 2026-10-24) added section 18, the UART as another
JieLi chip's open driver sets it up (SDK63), for Q-12 and Q-20, which stay
open.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **other chip (SDK63)**: the source is a JieLi SDK for different chips
    (SDK63), whose peripheral looks like the FM-1's chip's. A strong hint,
    never a confirmation for the FM-1's chip: the two chips are known to
    differ elsewhere (HW-75).
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image"); E-1: the block's first word is
  `0x01C7FC40`, the other 15 words 0; RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §3 (a pointer
  in r0 at the hand-over).
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

### HW-5: The code window and the flash chip
- Fact: In fwtest, the code window shows the 1 MiB flash chip from chip
  offset `0x4000`: window address `0x02000000 + n` reads chip offset
  `0x4000 + n`. At the start fwtest writes the image into the chip at
  offset `0x4000`, so the window's first bytes are the image and the bytes
  past it are the rest of the chip. With no `--flash` file the rest is
  erased and reads `0xFFFFFFFF`. Writes to the window are ignored; changes
  made to the chip through SPI0 show through the window (HW-47).
- Sources: HARNESS ("The raw image": the flash chip, past the image,
  writes to the window); E-1: the first word past the image and the word
  4 KiB further both read `0xFFFFFFFF`.
- Standing: confirmed (E-1)
- Needed by: M0d

### HW-6: Main RAM on the chip
- Fact: On the chip, main RAM is 512 KiB at `0x01C00000` to `0x01C7FFFF`.
  Its top 512 bytes, from `0x01C7FE00`, hold the interrupt vector table
  (HW-18), and the word at `0x01C7FFF8` inside it is also core 1's start
  address (HW-9). Below the table the SDK's own layout reserves
  `0x01C7FD4C` to `0x01C7FDFF` (52 bytes of boot information, then 128
### HW-46: When fwtest takes the samples, and what it measures
- Fact: In fwtest, a half's words are read from RAM at the moment that half
  finishes playing, so they must be complete by then: refill a half while
  the other plays. `ipb.csv` has one row per finished half, with the
  instructions each core ran since the previous one (HARNESS, "Outputs").
- Sources: HARNESS ("ipb.csv"); the emulator model (when the words are
  read); E-9.
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M4

## 8. Flash storage (M7, preliminary)

Later: only what fwtest presents. M7 should ask for more through spec
requests.

### HW-47: The flash chip, in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest the flash chip is a 1 MiB SPI NOR chip on SPI0
  (`JL_SPI0`, `0x00011C00`: `CON` +0, `BUF` +8). Its chip select is PD0,
  bit 0 of `JL_PORTD->OUT` (`0x000500C0`), low to select; each command is
  sent while selected and ends when PD0 goes high. A write to `BUF` sends
  one byte; with `CON` bit 12 set the byte received lands in `BUF`. `CON`
  bit 15 reads 1 when a byte is done; writing bit 14 clears it. The chip
  answers JEDEC ID `0x85 0x60 0x14` and understands the common SPI NOR
  commands read `0x03`, fast read `0x0B`, status `0x05`/`0x35`, write
  enable/disable `0x06`/`0x04`, 4 KiB erase `0x20`, 64 KiB erase `0xD8`,
  page program `0x02` (committed when PD0 goes high). Erase and program
  finish at once and the status never reports busy. Changes show through
  the code window (HW-5). Preliminary: M7 should confirm the chip and its
  timing through a spec request (a datasheet for the part).
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 548-557, 272 (`JL_SPI0`, `JL_PORTD`); RE
  `docs/io/09-storage.md` §1 (the flash is on SPI0; `CON` bits 15 and 14);
  HARNESS ("The flash chip", "Past the image"); the emulator model (JEDEC
  ID, chip select, commands, timing).
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M7

## 9. TIMER0 to TIMER3, corrected (M1)

### HW-48: TIMER0 to TIMER3, and what the acknowledge does in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest, `JL_TIMERn->CON` bits 0-1 non-zero run timer n (n = 0
  to 3); `CON` bits 4-7 select a prescaler of the 24 MHz clock. The timer
  counts up from `CNT` and, on reaching `PRD`, raises interrupt source
  4 + n and starts again from 0. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 while pending;
  writing `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. That acknowledging write also
  restarts the count, from the value last written to `CNT` (0 after an
  interrupt), and the period from the moment of the write. So in fwtest the
  time between
  two interrupts is `PRD` prescaled counts plus the time from the interrupt
  to the write that acknowledges it: with prescaler setting 2 and `PRD`
  1500, 24 000 time-base ticks (HW-13) plus about 1 tick when the handler
  acknowledges first, and more when it acknowledges later. This is fwtest,
  not a firmware setting: the period does not depend on anything but `PRD`,
  the prescaler and where the acknowledge sits. Whether the chip restarts
  the count on the acknowledge is Q-13. On the chip, the SDK names the
  prescaler settings 0 to 15 as dividing by 1, 4, 16, 64, 2, 8, 32, 128,
  256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768; in fwtest only setting 2
  (16) was measured (Q-3). Supersedes HW-16, which said the count starts
  again from 0 on reaching `PRD` without saying what the acknowledge does.
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 42-45 (`IRQ_TIMER0_IDX` 4 to `IRQ_TIMER3_IDX`
  7); SDK `apps/common/example/peripheral/timer/test2.c` lines 58-75 (the
  prescaler table); E-3 (the 1 ms period, `CON` read `0x8021` in the

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors the parts of JieLi's AC79 SDK we use, from a pinned commit, and
# checks every file against vendor/jieli-sdk/SHA256SUMS (PROVENANCE P-2).

#   tools/fetch-sdk.sh --verify   check the committed files (default, offline)
#   tools/fetch-sdk.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit into
#                                 vendor/jieli-sdk/, then verify
#

# hash to SHA256SUMS in the same commit, and log it in PROVENANCE.md.

"

DEST="$ROOT/vendor/jieli-sdk"
SUMS="$DEST/SHA256SUMS"

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1

}

verify() {
    status=0

    while read -r want path; do

        if [ ! -f "$DEST/$path" ]; then
            echo "MISSING $path"; status=1; continue
        fi

# 09 — Storage: NOR flash driver, norfs/FAT filesystems, VM key-value store, DX7 patches, firmware update

Target: M-Vave FM-1, JieLi AC791N/WL82. One external SPI NOR flash holds everything:
the firmware XIP image, a small NOR-resident file area ("sdfile"/norfs), a FAT/exFAT
volume, the VM (virtual-memory EEPROM-emulation) key-value area used by syscfg, and the
raw DX7 bank/patch region. Confidence: **high** = proven, **med** = strong inference,
**low** = guess.

Primary evidence: `analysis/shards/shard_020847aa_020847f2.txt`,
`shard_02084824_0208c3b4.txt` (SPI0/flash low level),
`shard_02002154_02003b52.txt` (ROM-call read/write cores),
`shard_02027346_02028fc6.txt` (flash ioctl, device framework, update file open),
`shard_02028fd2_0202b3d6.txt` + `shard_0202b498_0202e0fa.txt` + `shard_0202e108_0203091c.txt`
(FAT/VFS), `shard_02030942_02033964.txt` (VM KV), `shard_02019e9e_0201f07e.txt`
(DX7 pack/store), `shard_02082d14_0208478a.txt` (ufw/jlfs).

---

## 1. NOR flash driver (SPI0)

**SPI0 base `0x11C00`** (jielie `spi.md`: CON+0, BUF+8; CON bit15 PND, bit14 PCLR).
Low-level (all high conf):

| addr | name | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x020847AA` | `spi0_wait_ok` | poll `[0x11C00]` sign bit (PND) with 50 000 000-iteration timeout, clear via `\|= 0x4000`; returns 0 ok / −1 timeout |
| `0x020847DA` | `spi0_send_byte` | set TX direction (`\|= 8`, clear bit 12), `[0x11C00+8] = byte`, wait, restore |
| `0x0208478A` | `norflash_cs` | CS low/high helper (r0 = 0/1) |
| `0x02084700` | `norflash_spi0_guard` | wait SFC idle, save/restore SPI0 CON around bit-banged phases |
| `0x020847F2` | `norflash_enter_4byte_addr` | if flash size `[0x1C20190+24] > 16 MB` and addr ≥ 16 MB: one-shot **EN4B `0xB7`** |

**Command-mode engine `norflash_cs_and_erase` `0x02084BBE`** (med): enters SFC command
mode via SFR **`0x40200`** — saves `[0x1C20190+56]`, programs SPI0 CON from
`[0x1C20190+60]`, sets `[0x5101C] |= 0x20`, waits `0x40200` sign bit clear, issues the
command. The merged cluster around it contains:

- **page program**: WREN (`0x02084824` + verify `0x02084862`), opcode `0x02`,
  3/4-byte address via `spiflash_send_addr` `0x02084872`, byte loop, wait-ready
  `0x020848D0`, icache sync `0x02084B88` — at `0x02084C24`;
- **read**: dispatch `spiflash_io_dispatch` `0x02084A30` (single/dual/quad by chip type);
- **erase** at `0x02084D4E`: selector − 200 → `tbb` table —
  4 kB sector (`0x20`), 64 kB block (`0xD8`), whole chip (`0xC7`), 256-byte page
  (`0x81`, **med**); bounds-checked against `[0x1C20190+24]` flash size;
- **JEDEC ID** `0x9F` → 3 bytes into `[0x1C20190+28]`; **unique ID** `0x4B`
  (4 dummy + 16 UID bytes) — at `0x02084CC6`.

**Normal (memory-mapped) data path** — the CPU reads flash XIP, writes/erases go
through mask-ROM services (high):

| addr | name | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x0200372C` | `norflash_read_core` | mutex `0x1C0E670+2196` (`os_mutex_pend` `0x0205AE98`), bounds vs `[0x1C20190+24]`, reads in ≤256 B chunks via ROM **`0xFFC00404`** |
| `0x020037B4` | `norflash_read` | public wrapper, returns 0 on short read |
| `0x0200380A` | `norflash_write_core` | ROM **`0xFFC00476`**; then re-scrambles any data in the encrypted region (`< [0x1C20190+36]`) with the boot key `h[0x1C7FD50+28]` via the LFSR cipher `0x020037C8` |
| `0x020038A2` | `norflash_write` | public wrapper, 0 on failure |
| `0x02001D33A` | `norflash_ioctl` | device ioctl: erase/write/cache-control commands, mutex-guarded (cmd 206 = query VM area, used by `vm_area_init`) |
| `0x02028BA2` | `norflash_dev_init` | JEDEC read, capacity = 2^n, registers the device into the framework |

---

## 2. Filesystems

Two stacks share the flash through the device framework (devices `'norflash'`
`0x02055780`, `'nor_sdfile'` `0x0205572D`, `'sdfile_fat'` `0x02055738`, `'ramfs'`
`0x0204EAEC`, `'virtual'` `0x0204EC40`).

### 2.1 norfs — the "sdfile" NOR area (med)

A tiny JieLi filesystem of **CRC'd 32-byte directory entries** directly on NOR flash:

- `norfs_fopen` `0x020286A0` — resolve path → 40 B file object (`norfs_file_obj_init`
  `0x02028220`), trailing read/write/seek/close ops;
- `norfs_path_find` `0x0202852C`, `norfs_dir_find_entry` `0x020283D0`,
  `norfs_entry_scan` `0x0202847A` (≤32 entries, crc16 + name match),
  `norfs_addr_remap` `0x020283B4`;
- FM-1 content: `mnt/sdfile/app/usr` `0x0204F0A1`, `mnt/sdfile/app/btif` `0x0204F12E`,
  `mnt/sdfile/app/cfg_tool.bin` `0x0204F33C`, `res.bin` `0x0204EC48` (UI resources,
  read through `ui_res_read` `0x020100CE` with read-ahead cache).

### 2.2 FAT12/16/32 + exFAT (FatFS-derived, extended)

| addr | name | notes | conf |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x02029352` | `mount_volume` | parse BPB; exFAT detected via OEM field at +67 (`u32` + `'T'` byte check, `0x02029374..0x0202939C`); FAT12/16/32 by cluster count | high |
| `0x02029210` | `mount_alloc_fs` | allocate + link FATFS object, query sector count | med |
| `0x0202AEF8` | `fatfs_obj_alloc` | 812-byte filesystem work object | low |
| `0x020292FC` | `move_window` | sync then load sector into the FAT window | high |
| `0x0202C19A` | `fatfs_open` | open/create by path, truncate + exFAT handling | med |
| `0x0202CA26` | `fatfs_fopen` | mode-string (`r`/`w`/`rb`) front-end | med |
| `0x02029762` | `f_mkfs` | format: pick geometry, write BPB/FAT/root | high |
| `0x0202E1E2` | `fat_dir_walk` | recursive walk: attr filter, wildcard, callback, path stack | med |
| `0x0202FE2E` | `fat_ioctl` | **22-case** FS_IOCTL dispatcher (lfn buffers, dir info, seek) | high |
| `0x0202EC6A` | `fat_fsel` | file-select dispatcher: first/next/prev/num/path + cycle modes — the patch/bank browser primitive | high |
| `0x0202B96C` | `exfat_build_entry_set` | build 0x85/0xC0/0xC1 entries + name hash | high |
| `0x0202B7C8` / `0x0202B7F2` / `0x0202B8EA` | exfat entry-set checksum / verify / write | rotate-add checksum skipping bytes 2-3 | high/med |
| `0x0202B53A` … `0x0202BCF2` | FAT name/LFN helpers | 8.3 convert `0x0202B5E6`, LFN create `0x0202BCDE`, shortname checksum `0x0202BCBE` | high |

---

## 3. VM flash key-value store (syscfg backend)

JieLi's EEPROM-emulation "VM" layer: a ping-pong pair of flash sectors holding
append-only records, ids 0..255.

- **`vm_area_init` `0x02032140`**: gets the area from `norflash_ioctl(206)`; region
  size ≤ 8 kB or 16 kB by type; splits it in half — two sector bases at
  `[0x1C0E670+9252]` and `+9264`, half-size at `+9256`; **512-byte record offset cache**
  at `0x1C0E670+9276` (256 halfwords, one per id, `0x02032226..0x0203223C`);
  then `vm_mount_scan` `0x02027858`.
- **Sector magics**: first word of a sector is **`0x55AAAA54`** when freshly
  formatted/active and **`0xDDEEAA54`** for the retiring side
  (`0x02032294..0x020322AC`; written by `vm_sector_format` `0x0202707C`, swapped by
  `vm_garbage_collect` `0x02027112`, maintenance entry `vm_maintenance_locked`
  `0x02027292`) — conf med.
- **`vm_read` `0x0203249C`** (`id`, `buf`, `buflen`): id < 256 (`vm_id_valid`
  `0x02032490`); cached record offset `h[0x1C0E670+9276+id*2]`; active sector selected
  by state byte bit 1 (`b[0x1C0E670+9874]`); record = **4-byte header** {check byte,
  flags, 12-bit length at bits 4..15} + payload; integrity via the hardware CRC unit
  (`chip_crc16` `0x020025DA`, SFR `0x13500`), masked compare at `0x02032550`;
  errors −508/−510/−512; mutex `0x1C0E670+9788`.
- Writes: `vm_chunk_write` `0x02076B7A` (32-byte chunks through the flash device
  vtable), `vm_store_cursor_adjust` `0x02076B60`; GC relocates live records and swaps
  the ping-pong sector (`0x02027112`).
- **syscfg sits on top**: `syscfg_read` `0x02002612` / `syscfg_write` `0x020032B8`
  dispatch config items through a registered ops table (SYS, high).

---

## 4. DX7 patch storage

- The live edit buffer is the 155-byte VCED at **`0x1C0E670+5608`**.
- **`dx7voice_pack_store` `0x0201D532`** (high): packs VCED → 128-byte DX7 VMEM on the
  stack, then writes it to flash:
  - 6 ops × 21 bytes → 6 × 17 bytes with visible bit-packing (rates/levels merged,
    `0x0201D562..0x0201D5C8`); loop until 126 input bytes;
  - +9 pitch-EG bytes → VMEM+102; packed byte at +111; 4 LFO bytes at +112; packed
    sync/feedback byte at +116; +1 at +117; 10-byte name at +118 (total 128);
  - store address = `[0x1C0E670+256]` (bank base, set from board config) +
    `b[0x1C0E670+4778] << 7` (voice slot × 128), via `norflash_read` `0x02003712`
    (read-modify) + `norflash_write` `0x020037B4`, 128 bytes;
  - marker `b[0x1C0E670+5763] = 63` set first.
- The bank save UI is the menu page with string **`'  Dx7 32 Voice Save To ...  '`**
  `0x0204F3AE` — 32 voices × 128 B = one 4 kB sector per bank, matching the 0x20
  sector-erase granularity (med).
- Loading: `dx7patch_select_apply` `0x0201DAB8` — select patch: load, unpack, apply
  params, show name.

---

## 5. Firmware update (ufw / jlfs / OTA)

- **`jieli_ufw_update_run` `0x02082D24`**: allocates a 580-byte context
  (`mspace_malloc` `0x0205672E`), 1024-byte block buffer; checks the file-type magic
  (compares against **`0x5A04` / `0x5A08`** at `0x02082D84..0x02082D98`);
  `jieli_update_dispatch` `0x02083394` covers types **`0x5A02..0x5A08`**;
  `jieli_update_file_check` `0x0208332A` deletes or format-and-hangs on mismatch;
  progress callback through `[0x1C0E670+608]`.
- Package entries located from a 3-entry × 32-byte name table at `0x0204E4A4`
  (`0x02082DAC..0x02082DEE`), each name decrypted with **`jl_sfc_cipher` `0x020824FA`**
  (XOR stream, `key ^ (offset>>2)` per 32-byte block) and CRC-checked
  (`cfg_header_crc_check` `0x02026F8E`).
- Update file names (rodata `0x02082365..`): `Zedr_ota2.bin`, `Zsd_update2.bin`,
  `Zble_app_ota.bin`, `Zspp_app_ota.bin`, `Zusb_update2.bin`, `Zble_ota.bin`,
  `Zuart_user.bin`, `Znor_ota.bin`, `Znet_ota.bin`, `Zusb_hid_ota.bin` `0x02082419`,
  `ota.bin` `0x0208243A`; `LOADER.BIN` `0x02055831`.
- **jlfs** (JieLi library FS) package verify: `jlfs_entry_find_load` `0x020829F2` —
  find 32-byte entry by name, decrypt + CRC-verify payload; reader context
  `update_ctx_alloc` `0x020824AE` (104 B), `update_state_notify` `0x020824DE`.
- **OTA/update callback**: `update_state_callback` `0x02027EE2` — builds a 15-byte
  status record (leading bytes `89,48,8` …, one's-complement checksum tail) into
  `0x1C0E810+396`, posts `sys_event`, and resets on completion; the update-mode device
  path comes from `update_file_open` `0x02028998` (opens on the `'usb_update_mode'`
  `0x02055762` device, verifies entry CRCs). Firmware id string **`'FM-1_009'`**
  `0x0204F241`; ufw magic fragment `'"3DUfw'` `0x0204EF3E`.

---

## 6. Recovered storage interfaces

- `vm_read 0x0203249C(id, buffer, length)` returns a stored record length or a
  negative status. `vm_id_valid 0x02032490` restricts IDs to values below 256.
- `vm_chunk_write 0x02076B7A` appends a four-byte-header record while holding
  the VM mutex at `ENG+9788`; `syscfg_write 0x020032B8` dispatches through the
  higher-level configuration backends.
- `norflash_write 0x020038A2` reaches the low-level write path, while erase
  operations use 4 KiB granularity. `norflash_write_core 0x0200380A` applies
  transformation rules around the encrypted-region boundary stored at
  `[0x01C20190+36]`.
- `fatfs_fopen 0x0202CA26`, `norfs_fopen 0x020286A0`, and
  `fat_fsel 0x0202EC6A` expose the file and directory operations used by the
  application.

These are internal stock-firmware entry points, not stable APIs. In particular,
the inferred free regions and encryption boundary have not been validated as
safe targets for external writes.

  `0x02032490`); cached record offset `h[0x1C0E670+9276+id*2]`; active sector selected
  by state byte bit 1 (`b[0x1C0E670+9874]`); record = **4-byte header** {check byte,
  flags, 12-bit length at bits 4..15} + payload; integrity via the hardware CRC unit
  (`chip_crc16` `0x020025DA`, SFR `0x13500`), masked compare at `0x02032550`;
  errors −508/−510/−512; mutex `0x1C0E670+9788`.
- Writes: `vm_chunk_write` `0x02076B7A` (32-byte chunks through the flash device
  vtable), `vm_store_cursor_adjust` `0x02076B60`; GC relocates live records and swaps
  the ping-pong sector (`0x02027112`).
- **syscfg sits on top**: `syscfg_read` `0x02002612` / `syscfg_write` `0x020032B8`
  dispatch config items through a registered ops table (SYS, high).

---

## 4. DX7 patch storage

- The live edit buffer is the 155-byte VCED at **`0x1C0E670+5608`**.
- **`dx7voice_pack_store` `0x0201D532`** (high): packs VCED → 128-byte DX7 VMEM on the
  stack, then writes it to flash:
  - 6 ops × 21 bytes → 6 × 17 bytes with visible bit-packing (rates/levels merged,
    `0x0201D562..0x0201D5C8`); loop until 126 input bytes;
  - +9 pitch-EG bytes → VMEM+102; packed byte at +111; 4 LFO bytes at +112; packed
    sync/feedback byte at +116; +1 at +117; 10-byte name at +118 (total 128);
  - store address = `[0x1C0E670+256]` (bank base, set from board config) +
    `b[0x1C0E670+4778] << 7` (voice slot × 128), via `norflash_read` `0x02003712`
    (read-modify) + `norflash_write` `0x020037B4`, 128 bytes;
  - marker `b[0x1C0E670+5763] = 63` set first.
- The bank save UI is the menu page with string **`'  Dx7 32 Voice Save To ...  '`**
  `0x0204F3AE` — 32 voices × 128 B = one 4 kB sector per bank, matching the 0x20
  sector-erase granularity (med).
- Loading: `dx7patch_select_apply` `0x0201DAB8` — select patch: load, unpack, apply
  params, show name.

---

## 5. Firmware update (ufw / jlfs / OTA)

- **`jieli_ufw_update_run` `0x02082D24`**: allocates a 580-byte context
  (`mspace_malloc` `0x0205672E`), 1024-byte block buffer; checks the file-type magic
  (compares against **`0x5A04` / `0x5A08`** at `0x02082D84..0x02082D98`);
  `jieli_update_dispatch` `0x02083394` covers types **`0x5A02..0x5A08`**;
  `jieli_update_file_check` `0x0208332A` deletes or format-and-hangs on mismatch;
  progress callback through `[0x1C0E670+608]`.
- Package entries located from a 3-entry × 32-byte name table at `0x0204E4A4`
  (`0x02082DAC..0x02082DEE`), each name decrypted with **`jl_sfc_cipher` `0x020824FA`**
  (XOR stream, `key ^ (offset>>2)` per 32-byte block) and CRC-checked
  (`cfg_header_crc_check` `0x02026F8E`).
- Update file names (rodata `0x02082365..`): `Zedr_ota2.bin`, `Zsd_update2.bin`,
  `Zble_app_ota.bin`, `Zspp_app_ota.bin`, `Zusb_update2.bin`, `Zble_ota.bin`,
  `Zuart_user.bin`, `Znor_ota.bin`, `Znet_ota.bin`, `Zusb_hid_ota.bin` `0x02082419`,
  `ota.bin` `0x0208243A`; `LOADER.BIN` `0x02055831`.
- **jlfs** (JieLi library FS) package verify: `jlfs_entry_find_load` `0x020829F2` —
  find 32-byte entry by name, decrypt + CRC-verify payload; reader context
  `update_ctx_alloc` `0x020824AE` (104 B), `update_state_notify` `0x020824DE`.
- **OTA/update callback**: `update_state_callback` `0x02027EE2` — builds a 15-byte
  status record (leading bytes `89,48,8` …, one's-complement checksum tail) into
  `0x1C0E810+396`, posts `sys_event`, and resets on completion; the update-mode device
  path comes from `update_file_open` `0x02028998` (opens on the `'usb_update_mode'`
  `0x02055762` device, verifies entry CRCs). Firmware id string **`'FM-1_009'`**
  `0x0204F241`; ufw magic fragment `'"3DUfw'` `0x0204EF3E`.

---

## 6. Recovered storage interfaces

- `vm_read 0x0203249C(id, buffer, length)` returns a stored record length or a
  negative status. `vm_id_valid 0x02032490` restricts IDs to values below 256.
- `vm_chunk_write 0x02076B7A` appends a four-byte-header record while holding
  the VM mutex at `ENG+9788`; `syscfg_write 0x020032B8` dispatches through the
  higher-level configuration backends.
- `norflash_write 0x020038A2` reaches the low-level write path, while erase
  operations use 4 KiB granularity. `norflash_write_core 0x0200380A` applies
  transformation rules around the encrypted-region boundary stored at
  `[0x01C20190+36]`.
- `fatfs_fopen 0x0202CA26`, `norfs_fopen 0x020286A0`, and
  `fat_fsel 0x0202EC6A` expose the file and directory operations used by the
  application.

These are internal stock-firmware entry points, not stable APIs. In particular,
the inferred free regions and encryption boundary have not been validated as
safe targets for external writes.

The firmware container is a **UFW** update package (chip "AC791N") holding

1. Mask ROM loads SPL from flash `0xA0` (XIP) and jumps in.
2. SPL (`uboot.boot`) sets up clocks/SDRAM-less defaults, reads the JLFS
   directory, maps the app area XIP at `0x02000000` and jumps to
   `0x020000A0`.
3. App CRT (`0x02000000`): set SP/SSP, zero `.bss`, copy `.data` from flash
   `0x02084820`, copy overlay to `0x04000120`, copy boot params to hwinfo
   `0x01C7FD50`.
4. `pll_clock_init 0x020000F8` → 240 MHz; `clock_board_init 0x02001AB0`
   (contains `0x02001C24` rate config).
5. Kernel init + `main` (`0x0200457A` neighborhood): initcall tables,
   `board_init 0x0200417E` (keys/ADC/SPI display/audio server at 44118 Hz),
   then task creation (`usr_app_task 0x02022CFE` = the UI app) and
  `0x1EEE008` accordingly.

The mask ROM loads `uboot.boot` (14,384 B) to RAM and runs it; its header contains
the load address `0x01C02000` (bytes at offset 4). The SPL:

- brings up the SPI-NOR flash and clocking sufficient for XIP,
- parses the `app_area_head` flash file table in the download container (entries for
  `app.bin`, `cfg_tool.bin`, plus `VM`/`PRCT`/`CODE`/`BTIF`/`AUTO`/`USR` section
  tags), and maps/verifies the app at XIP `0x02000000`,
- reads fields from the app vector area (e.g. the `ssp` value at `app+12`,
  `0x01C15BB4`) when preparing the handoff,
- jumps to `0x02000000` with a **boot-parameter struct pointer in `r0`**
  (consumed by `boot_hwinfo_save 0x020000C6`; the SPL side of the protocol is
  `[low]` — inferred from the app-side consumers).

Container metadata (`jlfw.yaml`) lists `entry-point: 33554720` = `0x02000120`, and
the CRT tail-jumps to `0x02001C24` — both exactly 0x120 above the reset vector
(`0x02000000`) and the bring-up function start (`0x02001B04`) respectively. See the
anomaly note in §5.

## 4. Exception/interrupt vector area (`0x02000098`–`0x020000C4`)

```
0x02000098  usp = 0x01C15EB4               ; cpu1 entry: user/system stack
0x0200009E  sp  = 0x01C16EB4
0x020000A4  reti = 0x01C023D6
0x020000AA  rti                            ; cpu1 starts by "returning" into RAM code
0x020000AC  trigger                        ; software-interrupt trigger instruction
0x020000B0  [--sp] = {sp,ssp,usp,icfg,psr,rets,retx,rete,reti}
0x020000B4  [--sp] = {r15-r0}              ; full 25-word context save
0x020000B8  r0 = sp
0x020000BC  call 0x020002A2                ; C dispatcher, r0 = saved-frame pointer
   called with 0..3 during this phase.

The task created by the boot continuation (§5.2) runs the main application state
machine from its node-table entry (fallback entry `0x0200473C`).

3:### HW-75: The UART as three other JieLi chips' open driver sets it up
4:- Fact: Three other JieLi chips, the ones SDK63 calls br23, br25 and
5:  bd29, have three UARTs with the FM-1's chip's eleven words in the same
6:  order, widths and access (HW-68), at the same three bases, and SDK63's
7:  drivers for them are open source. All three drivers do the same:
8:  - The rate: `BAUD` is f / baud rounded to the nearest whole number,
9:    divided by 4 (rounded down), less 1, where f is the UART clock; so
10:    the rate is f / (4 × (`BAUD` + 1)). For 31 250 baud that is 383 from a
11:    48 MHz clock and 191 from 24 MHz, both exact.
12:  - Set-up: the pending flags cleared (`CON0` bits 13, 12 and 10 written
55:  `include_lib/driver/cpu/br23/asm/clock_hw.h` line 298 (the UART clock
56:  field). For the FM-1's chip: SDK `WL82.h` lines 569-591; HW-53.
57:- Standing: other chip (SDK63)
58:- Needed by: real hardware (Level 2); M6a and M6b (the UART's set-up)
59:
60:## Open questions
61:
62:What isn't known, or is known only from material the spec may not use. A
63:spec request can turn one into a fact.
64:
65:- **Q-1. Other RAM on the chip.** Whether the chip has RAM at `0x01F00000`
66:  and `0x04000000` (HW-7), how much, and whether it can be used. The SDK's
67:  layout names a cache RAM at `0x01F20000` and an external SDRAM window at
68:  `0x04000000`.
69:- **Q-2. Clock set-up on the chip.** Which registers and steps set the PLL
70:  and system clock on real hardware (fwtest needs none). Since SR-2, the
71:  clock registers' addresses, the main clock select and the supported rates
72:  are known (HW-53, HW-54); still open: the PLL's control registers and
73:  fields (FM-1-RE places the PLL block at `0x00016A00`, which the SDK's
74:  header names as part of another block; the SDK's own PLL and `SYS_DIV`
75:  field definitions are switched off), the order of the steps that change
76:  the system clock safely (the flash and bus clocks with it), and the
77:  clock when an installed app starts: FM-1-RE says only that the loader
78:  brings up "clocking sufficient for XIP". Settled by a datasheet or a
79:  probe on real hardware.
80:- **Q-3. TIMER0-3 prescaler settings in fwtest.** The SDK gives the chip's
81:  table (HW-48); fwtest's settings other than 0 and 2 were not measured.
82:  Measure with a black-box test, or ask.
83:- **Q-4. The core tick timer's period on the chip.** Which clock `TTMR_PRD`
84:  counts on real hardware (fwtest always uses 10 ms).
85:- **Q-5. A debug console on the chip.** Whether `DBG_MSG` writes go
86:  anywhere on real hardware (the SDK marks it read-only, and reads it as
87:  the exception's cause word, HW-51), or which UART pins could carry debug
88:  output.
89:- **Q-6. LCD wiring.** Since SR-3, SPI1's pin groups, the pin-group
90:  select, the port set-up registers, `CON`'s named bits, the panel's clock
91:  limit and reset timing, and FM-1's own `CON` and `BAUD` values are known
92:  (HW-55 to HW-58); still open: which pin is the panel's chip select
93:  (probably PC7), whether the panel has a reset pin and a backlight pin,
94:  which ones and their levels; the drive the pins need; `CON` bit 5 and
95:  the other mode bits, and how `BAUD` sets the clock (so which value gives
96:  at most 15 MHz); the panel's offset within the controller's 240 × 320
97:  memory for each `MADCTL` orientation, which orientation shows the
98:  picture upright as the FM-1 is held, and whether it needs inversion on
99:  (`0x21`) to show colours right (none of the sources says; fwtest ignores
100:  `MADCTL` and inversion, HW-31). Settled by a probe on real hardware.
101:- **Q-7. The panel's wiring on the chip.** Whether the board's key matrix,
102:  encoders and LEDs are wired as fwtest presents them (HW-33, HW-34,
103:  HW-38, HW-42: the pins, the shift registers, an LED for every key, which
104:  physical turn is "clockwise"); pull-ups, directions and drive for the
105:  pins, LED polarity and current. fwtest needs no pin set-up.

# Verified rollback from a modified V15-derived build to stock V15 - 2026-09-04

I recovered my FM-1 from a locally modified firmware package back to stock V15 over USB. There is no official FM-1 V16 release involved here: the device reported version 16 only because my test package was derived from stock V15 and had its version identity intentionally bumped to 16 so the normal updater would accept the modified image.

That distinction matters. This recovery demonstrates that the FM-1 can be moved backward from a higher reported version identity to an older stock package when the application is still running and the update transport remains reachable. In this case, the modified package had also broken the normal USB configuration descriptor, but an already-active Windows descriptor filter still exposed the MIDI port.

The recovery failure turned out to be in the host response framing, not an anti-rollback fuse or permanent device-side downgrade block. The device's final 481-byte loader request got a reply declaring 488 body bytes while actually containing 489. The device checks that decoded length before dispatching the response, so it rejected the packet. Encoding the complete decoded message first and then packing it into MIDI-safe 7-bit bytes fixed the transfer. The same correction also applies to other partial-block requests.

The live run used a local Windows.Devices.Midi adapter. This PR brings the shared protocol corrections into the Linux client; it does not claim a hardware test of the ALSA transport. The adapter also needed to accept Windows' numbered port labels (`2 - USB-Midi`) and stock identity checksums. No Windows driver or replacement firmware is included here.

## What this proves

The successful rollback is evidence that, for this tested path, the version restriction enforced by the normal updater is at least partly host-side policy rather than a one-way device fuse. The device was running a V15-derived test build that identified itself as version 16, and the corrected client successfully supplied the stock V15 package, completed the normal OTA write, rebooted, and returned as stock V15.

This does not yet prove arbitrary rollback between every historical FM-1 release. Older packages may differ in metadata, loader behavior, or package layout and should still be checked before use. It also does not replace the lower-level JieLi USB_KEY/UBOOT recovery path for a hard brick where the application no longer runs or no usable update transport is reachable.

## Code path

```text
device requests logical offset + length
  -> slice that exact number of bytes from the stock package
  -> build [00 59 30][length+8][type][address][length][payload][checksum]
  -> pack the complete message into 7-bit MIDI bytes
  -> send the response
  -> acknowledge E0000000 / F0000000 with success\0
  -> verify the identity after the device returns
```

The complete header construction is visible in the existing
[vendor packet builder](../../analysis/host-updater/ota_worker_decomp.c#L1455),
`FUN_140017b20`. The device's length check is at V13 `0x02026BDA`/`0x02026BDC`
in the [vendor disassembly](../../analysis/disassembly/app_pi32v2_objdump.txt#L56222).

Stock V15 and its loader return a zero-padded plain identity, such as
`ota-FM-1_015`. The client now reads that format while retaining the older
encoded identity format. Stock replies use the one's-complement checksum.
My modified V15-derived test build reported `FM-1_016` but retained V15's checksum after the version digit was changed; the exception is limited to that exact captured response.

## Instrumentation and observed result

```text
read-only command: modified V15-derived test build reporting FM-1 V16 on 4C4A:C755
  -> hash-check the unchanged stock V15 package
  -> 48 staging data requests, then E0000000
  -> capture new USB identity 4D4A:4155
  -> command reply: ota-FM-1 V15
  -> 1167 flash data requests, then F0000000
  -> capture normal USB identity 4C4A:C755
  -> separate read-only command: FM-1 V15
  -> read raw USB descriptor: 293 bytes, valid walk
  -> Windows enumeration: FM-1 Audio OK, FM-1 Midi OK
```

The image was `FM-1_015`, 699956 bytes (699936 after removing FWSC markers),
SHA-256 `DB1642B2B6FA5C2CCCB11FFD13878068BB28601678D3644049F99DC40E7EDB8A`.
The post-boot configuration descriptor SHA-256 was
`8E5F630AEF8941ECDCC59628B616216D9C15AC25A1BB6A03A97C430A08614DBF`.

The [redacted record](../../tools/tests/fixtures/fm1-v15-reflash-2026-09-04.json)
preserves every requested address, length and flash type. Each run is
`[first_address, length, flash_type, count, address_stride]`; expanding the runs
reproduces all 49 first-stage and 1168 second-stage records, including their
terminal requests. The data-request counts exclude those terminal records.
It also contains the actual OTA identity reply and the separate post-boot
observations. Original logs were retained locally and checked against their
saved hash manifest before this allowlisted record was extracted. Host paths,
device-instance IDs, serials and firmware payloads are excluded.

## Check the evidence without touching hardware

From the repository root:

```sh
python tools/verify_reflash_record.py
python -m unittest discover -s tools/tests -v
```

The checker expands the captured requests, checks their bounds and counts,
requires both terminal signals and the separate post-boot V15 observation,
and decodes generated replies against the device's length/checksum contract.
With no firmware supplied, it uses synthetic zero payloads for the wire checks.
To replay the requested payload bytes from your own copy of the exact stock
package, still without opening MIDI ports:

```sh
python tools/verify_reflash_record.py --firmware path/to/FM-1_V15.fwsc
```

Expected first line:

```text
Recorded capture chain verified: FM-1 V16 -> OTA V15 -> flash complete -> FM-1 V15.
```

In that checker output, `FM-1 V16` is the captured identity of the locally modified V15-derived test package, not an official V16 firmware release.

That command checks the supplied record's consistency. It does not independently
authenticate a historical capture or perform another flash. The hardware result
comes from the recorded device observations. A terminal signal alone would not
establish the installed version; changing the recorded post-boot version back to
16 makes the check fail.

This was the stock OTA erase/write process, without a separate whole-chip wipe,
ROM recovery, flash readback or an audio playback test. The PC was not rebooted
and no elevation prompt was needed during the reflash; the device reset itself
through the normal update protocol. It is evidence for this unit and this path,
not interrupted-update safety or recovery from an application that cannot run.

content.content:
## The .fwsc logical image

Requests address a *logical* image, not the raw file:

- The first `20 × 0x30` (960) file bytes are the interleaved UFW header:
  each `0x30`-byte block carries `0x2F` data bytes + 1 marker byte. Strip the
  markers → 940 logical header bytes.
- Everything after offset 960 is raw.

So `logical = strip48(file[0:960]) + file[960:]` (704084 → 704064 bytes).
The UFW header decrypts (HDRKEY `0xFFFF`) to hdrcrc/listcrc/imgsize/numents
+ 8 entries: `flash.bin`, `info.log`, `USR`, `isd_config.ini`, `ota.bin`,
`script.ver`, `blimit.bin`, `tail.bin`. `script.ver` (SFC-encrypted, chipkey
`0x980F`) decrypts to `AC791N-v0.01-cfg_tool-v0.10`.

## Terminal signals and timing

Static decompilation of the 2026-07-06 M-UPGRADE worker confirms that the
terminal conditions are raw addresses, not flash types:

- `0xE0000000`, length 8: verification complete. Reply with `success\0`, keep
  the MIDI connection open for 3000 ms, then wait for re-enumeration.
- `0xF0000000`, length 8: loader finish request. Reply with `success\0`. Its
  receipt proves that the loader reached the post-write finish path, not that
  the requested version subsequently booted.

The worker sleeps 2000 ms after each upgrade command before reading requests,
and each receive has an 8000 ms timeout. It sends no keepalive or pre-finish
packet; those were artifacts of an earlier incorrect frame interpretation.

## syscmd core (normal-mode device control, cmd ids 17–48)

Separate from the OTA pull protocol: `serial_midi_task 0x02027AF4` →
`update_cmd_dispatch 0x02026BC4`, framing
`[00 59][cmd:1][len:3 LE][payload][~sum(payload)]`. V14 has the same
dispatcher at `0x0202730E` and the same 32-entry branch table.
must not be sent to the only recoverable device.

This is also distinct from the SDK's optional `new_cfg_tool.c` protocol. That
tool uses a `5A AA A5`/CRC16 frame over USB CDC and includes physical flash
read, erase, write, and MaskROM-entry commands. The signature is absent from
the V13/V14 applications, UBOOTs, and extracted OTA loaders, and stock normal
USB exposes no CDC interface. The packaged `cfg_tool.bin` is a data resource,
not evidence that this transport is linked or usable as recovery.

## Step-1 verifier — hardware-verified findings (2026-07-21)

Exhaustive on-device probing (build a fwsc, flash step-1, watch for the
`0xE0000000` verification-done signal / a soft reset) established:

- **The forced loader-replacement read-back is identical for payloads up to
  19456 bytes (0x4C00).** In these modified-package tests, the verifier wrote
  the incoming `ota.bin` payload to the loader flash region as plaintext and
  read it back for the payload CRC. Payloads of 64, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096,
  8192, 12288, 16384, 16896, 17408, 18432, and 19456 bytes passed. No
  scrambling was required, disproving the earlier SFC-descramble theory.
- **The tested replacement path rejects payloads above 19456 bytes.** A
  19456-byte payload passes and a 19457-byte payload fails. The stock loader's
  compressed payload is 19937 bytes (`dlen=0x4DE1`), 481 bytes above this
  observed staging limit, and its overflow tail did not read back correctly.
  This does not mean an ordinary stock update must replace the loader: the
  stock V13/V14 loader is identical, and bundled logs record a successful
  stock downgrade.
- **The tail is NOT descrambled with any known key.** 16 pre-scramble variants
  (plain jl_enc_cipher + jl_sfc_cipher with seeds 0x375F, 0x980F, 0xFFFF,
  0xFFFE, 0x0000, 0x0001, 0x035e, 0x1dbf, 0x31f0, 0x67ac, 0x68ff, 0xadde, and
  SFC bases 0/0x4000/0x94000/0x90000) all failed — so the overflow tail is
  write-dropped at the region limit (read-back = stale data), not descrambled.
- The seed `h[0x1C7FD6C]` (used by `FUNC_0200380a → FUNC_020037c8` for the
  encrypted-region read-back) is a per-chip OTP value read by the SPL from a
  companion die (see the SPL analysis); it is NOT needed for ≤ 19456-byte
  payloads and does not affect the > 19456 overflow.
- The result handler `FUNC_02027F88` resets into the loader **iff
  verifier-return==0 AND notify byte `b[0x1C0E670+60]==0`** — no other no-op
  gate after the CRC. The verifier clears notify on CRC success, so the CRC is

Requests address a *logical* image, not the raw file:

  markers → 940 logical header bytes.

The UFW header decrypts (HDRKEY `0xFFFF`) to hdrcrc/listcrc/imgsize/numents

Static decompilation of the 2026-07-06 M-UPGRADE worker confirms that the
terminal conditions are raw addresses, not flash types:
